notes: CORE facts only — tenant-neutral architecture truths valid for every Scout deployment and every domain package. Deployment-scoped facts (configured provider, model, deadline, hosting, provider allocations) are generated separately by lib/deployment-facts.js from actual configuration. Tenant-scoped scope claims live in each package's knowledge.systemFacts.

facts.text: Scout is a portable conversational intelligence and orchestration runtime. Deterministic components classify, route, resolve context and coreference, gather evidence, and enforce validation; the configured generative model writes the normal visible answer from a semantic response contract and verified evidence. Capabilities such as retrieval, tenant-knowledge access, computation, memory, and workflows are optional and may or may not be enabled in a given deployment or domain package. Retrieval is used when relevant and available; it is not what defines Scout.

Generated answers are validated before they are shown: claims are checked against evidence and entity relationships, unsupported or overclaimed statements are rejected, and bounded generative recovery may repair a failed answer. If validation cannot produce a supported answer, the response fails closed rather than inventing facts.

Evidence in Scout is typed by provenance: tenant knowledge evidence, computed facts, tool results, user input, and general reasoning are kept distinct so validators can tell what kind of support a claim has.

A Scout application is Scout Core plus a domain package: tenant identity, tenant knowledge, policies, capability allow/deny lists, and optional workflows. Scout Core with no domain package is General Scout — a first-class configuration with conversation, computation, and session state, where domain-specific claims resolve as unknown instead of being invented.

Executable capabilities are governed by a bounded action runtime: the active package's allow-list is enforced at the execution boundary, permission scopes are checked, side-effecting actions require a verified one-time confirmation grant, arguments are validated, every call is deadline-bounded, and every attempt is audited. Package data can never grant scopes, register handlers, or raise the request deadline.

Scout telemetry can report the prose source, provider, model, provider-call count, input and output tokens, actual or estimated usage units, model latency, repair attempts, retrieval candidate count, selected evidence count, and session totals when available. MODEL_GENERATION means a model authored the visible answer; DIRECT_KB means verified knowledge supplied the answer without a generative model call; TECHNICAL_ERROR means generation or factual validation failed closed.
